title: Design System: Rasha Al Haj Hasan — Portfolio

hairline.note: Decorative rules only (1.3–1.5:1); never the sole sign of a state.

bordeaux-thread.note: Decorative lines only in dark mode (2.7:1 on the dark canvas).

bordeaux-text.note: Accent text and every interactive state: focus ring, current page, hover underline. ≥6.1:1 in both themes.

display.purpose: The name in the Home hero only.

headline.purpose: Page titles, each followed by one script word.

title.purpose: Role titles, featured project titles, empty-state headings, About headline; 400, or 500 where it aids scanning.

subtitle.purpose: Skill-group names, glance and summary terms, card titles in dense grids, short emphasis (500).

lead.purpose: Page intros, hero tagline and bio paragraphs; keep to about 42rem.

label.purpose: Tracked uppercase labels and section-rule titles; 12px and untracked in Arabic.

script.purpose: One decorative, aria-hidden word per page header.

shadows.name: device
shadows.purpose: Hardware mock-ups in the hero showcase only.

shadows.name: chip
shadows.purpose: Technology chips floating beside the devices.

motion.name: reveal
motion.value: opacity 0→1, translateY 10px→0, 500ms, once on entering the viewport
motion.purpose: Content blocks as they scroll in.

motion.name: hover-color
motion.purpose: Colour and border changes on hover.

motion.name: nav-underline
motion.purpose: Active-page underline moving between desktop links.

motion.name: gallery
motion.purpose: Screenshot viewer overlay and image changes; previous/next follow the reading direction.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: Framer Motion reducedMotion='user' (opacity only) + CSS animations/transitions ≈0ms
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: no movement, scale, typing, resizing, blinking or smooth scroll.

focusRing.purpose: Every :focus-visible state. Bordeaux Text keeps ≥3:1 in both themes.

narrative.overview:
The site reads like a working developer's journal: real code and real devices on the opening page, each page header signed with one handwritten word, and every page framed in an orderly editorial grid of hairline rules, numbered sections and small tracked labels. The working parts are shown, from the code editor in the hero to the typed localhost address, but the frame around them stays calm, so the work reads as considered rather than busy.

It is warm and personal, not corporate. The warmth comes from three quiet sources rather than from colour or decoration: a single Bordeaux Thread that marks Rasha's presence (the dot after her name, the active-page underline, section numbers, the focus ring), one script word per page that feels written by hand, and generous space that lets each fact breathe. Everything else is Studio Grey, Paper White and Graphite.

Density is low and unhurried: one idea per row, long line-height, wide gutters. The system holds its character in English and Arabic, light and dark, from a 320px phone to a wide desktop, and with whatever content the Google Sheet currently holds. Sparse content is normal, and the layout should look intentional with a single item as much as with ten. Accessibility is part of the identity, not a layer on top: every state the Bordeaux Thread marks must also be readable, operable by keyboard and calm under reduced motion.

Items marked Pending describe the target behaviour where today's code differs; implement them before treating the rule as met.
keyCharacteristics: Cool grey canvas, white working surfaces, graphite type, one burgundy accent.
Light-weight Jost display type (300), regular body (400), medium (500) for titles, labels and buttons.
Structure drawn with 1px hairlines and numbered section rules, not boxes and fills.
Pill-shaped controls and tags; gently rounded (6px) cards.
Physical objects (phone, laptop, browser) are the only things that cast real shadows.
Fully mirrored right-to-left in Arabic, using logical properties throughout.
WCAG 2.2 AA in both themes and both languages.

rules.name: The One Thread Rule
rules.body: Bordeaux is for graphics, rules, dots, numbers, small labels and interactive states, never for body text, headings or large fills. The single permitted fill is the Home contact band, the one moment the thread widens into a ribbon.

rules.name: The Accessible Thread Rule
rules.body: When Bordeaux signals a state (focus, current page, hover, selection), it is Bordeaux Text, never Bordeaux Thread, so the cue clears 3:1 in both themes. It accompanies a second cue (underline, border, weight, icon or fill change) and is never the only sign of the state. One Bordeaux cue per element at a time. Pending: four state cues currently use Bordeaux Thread, which is 2.7:1 in dark mode: the focus outline, the desktop active-page underline, the Projects filter-chip hover border and the Contact channel icon's hover border. Switch all four to Bordeaux Text.

rules.name: The Theme Pair Rule
rules.body: Every colour is a role token with a light and a dark value. Hard-coded colours are allowed only for physical objects (bezels, editor chrome and syntax colours, the gallery's dark backdrop) and for content placed on the burgundy band.

rules.name: The Light Display Rule
rules.body: Display and headline sizes stay Light (300); hierarchy at the top of a page comes from size, not weight. Medium (500) is the weight for scanning and structure: subtitles, titles that sit in dense rows, labels, buttons and short emphasis. Body text stays Regular (400). 600 is loaded but not used; reach for size or spacing before reaching for it.

rules.name: The One Script Word Rule
rules.body: The script face appears once per page, beside the page title (plus the single script line in the hero and the contact band). It is decorative and aria-hidden, and it never carries information.

rules.name: The Joined Letters Rule
rules.body: Arabic text is never letter-spaced (tracking breaks the joins) and gets a taller line-height (1.9) for paragraphs and list items. Arabic at 14px or smaller may step up to 500 for legibility; it never goes below 12px.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn with 1px Hairline rules (top/bottom borders and dividers), not with filled boxes. Reach for a rule before a background.

rules.name: The Numbered Section Rule
rules.body: Sections open with a section rule: a Bordeaux number ("01"), a tracked label, a hairline that fills the row, and an optional action link at the end. Numbers count only the sections actually shown.

rules.name: The Mirror Rule
rules.body: Every layout is checked in Arabic at 320px and at desktop width before it ships. If something has to be written twice (once for LTR, once for RTL), it is probably using a physical property where a logical one belongs.

rules.name: The Objects-Cast-Shadows Rule
rules.body: Physical objects cast real shadows; interface surfaces get, at most, a soft lift for state.

dos: Do use role tokens (`canvas`, `surface`, `ink`, `line`, `wine`, `wine-text`) so every new element works in light and dark at once.
Do draw structure with 1px Hairline rules and numbered section rules before reaching for boxes or fills.
Do use Bordeaux Text for every interactive state (focus ring, current page, hover underline) and pair it with a second cue (The Accessible Thread Rule).
Do set display and headline in Jost Light (300), body in Regular (400), and use Medium (500) for titles, subtitles, labels and buttons where it helps scanning.
Do give each new page header one script word, aria-hidden.
Do use logical properties (start/end), mirror directional icons, and check every layout in Arabic at 320px and at desktop width, with technology names, emails and URLs kept left-to-right.
Do design every content block for one item, many items, a missing field and a missing translation, and give every list a loading skeleton and an empty state.
Do keep controls as pills at least 44px tall (header controls 36px), with a visible 2px focus ring.
Do respect reduced motion: opacity-only transitions, no typing or resizing, nothing that blinks.
donts: Don't set body text, headings or long passages in Bordeaux, use Bordeaux Thread as a state indicator in dark mode, or add a second accent colour.
Don't signal a state with colour alone or with a Hairline-coloured border alone.
Don't add shadows to interface surfaces at rest. Real shadows belong to physical objects, and lift is for hover or floating state only.
Don't use weight 600 or above, set display or headline text heavier than 300, or letter-space Arabic text.
Don't use the script face for information, navigation or more than one word per page header.
Don't hard-code colours outside physical objects and the contact band.
Don't show empty placeholders, error codes or broken images: hide what is missing and use the designed fallback states.
Don't use physical left/right properties outside the device stage, or mirror icons that are not directional.
Don't add automatic motion without a pause mechanism, or motion that ignores reduced-motion settings.
